title: should / shouldn't — Giving Advice
grammarNote:
"Should" — модальный глагол для советов и рекомендаций. Это вежливый мягкий способ выразить мнение.

① Совет (advice):
   "You should see a doctor." (Тебе следует сходить к врачу.)
   "She should get more sleep." (Ей стоит больше спать.)
   "You shouldn't eat so much sugar." (Не следует.)

② Рекомендация:
   "You should try the beshbarmak here — it's amazing!"

③ Ожидание:
   "The package should arrive tomorrow." (ожидаю)

④ Should have (прошлое — критика):
   "I should have studied more." (нужно было — но не учил)
   "You shouldn't have said that." (не стоило)

🔧 Образование: Subject + should + base verb (без to!)
"She should go." ✅ · "She should to go." ❌
Should НИКОГДА не меняется: she should, he should (без -s!)

grammarTable.subject: I / You / He / She / It / We / They
grammarTable.example: You should study every day. She should ask the lecturer.

grammarTable.subject: I / You / He / She / It / We / They
grammarTable.example: You shouldn't wait until the last minute.

grammarTable.subject: QUESTION: Should + subject + BASE?
grammarTable.example: Should I email the lecturer? Should she visit the office?

grammarTable.subject: SHORT ANSWER positive
grammarTable.example: Should I go? — Yes, you should.

grammarTable.subject: SHORT ANSWER negative
grammarTable.example: Should I worry? — No, you shouldn't.

grammarTable.subject: MEANING: recommendation
grammarTable.example: You should drink more water. (advice, not a rule)

grammarTable.subject: MEANING: expectation / mild duty
grammarTable.example: Students should arrive on time. (expected behaviour)

grammarTable.subject: STRUCTURE: always BASE form after
grammarTable.example: She should go ✓ / She should goes ✗ / She should to go ✗

rows.example: You should talk to your lecturer about the problem.
You should try the new café near campus — the coffee is amazing!
Students should show respect to all staff members.
You should turn left at the library, then go straight.

rows.form: Expressing obligation that is moral, not legal
rows.example: You should apologise — you were rude to her.
"I think you should talk to Amir about this. He always gives good advice."
She shoulds go. ✗ → She should go. ✓
You should to study. ✗ → You should study. ✓
He should studying. ✗ → He should study. ✓
You should not to go. ✗ → You shouldn't go. ✓

rows.form: "Should" is for advice, not strong obligation
rows.example: If it's a rule, use "must": You must attend 80% of classes. (not "should")
Do you should go? ✗ → Should you go? ✓
You should eat breakfast. (it's a good idea — your choice)
You must attend 80% of classes. (it's a rule — you have no choice)

rows.form: "should" — breaking the advice has consequences but no punishment
rows.example: You should sleep 8 hours. (advice — you can ignore it, but you'll be tired)

rows.form: "must" — breaking the rule has clear consequences
rows.example: You must not cheat. (rule — if you break it, you may be expelled)
I should start my essay today. / I really should call my parents more often.
You should eat before the exam. / You should apologise to Zhibek.
I think you should talk to your academic advisor.
Maybe you should try again tomorrow.
You really should start preparing now.
Perhaps you shouldn't leave it to the last minute.
I've made a mistake — what should I do?
Should I email the lecturer or go in person?

grammarTip:
Шкала обязательности:
must → обязан (100%) — строгое требование
have to → должен (90%) — внешние правила
should → следует (60%) — совет, рекомендация
could → мог бы (40%) — слабый совет

💡 Should для совета — вежливо и мягко:
✅ "You should try meditation." (совет другу)
✅ "You should visit Charyn Canyon." (рекомендация)
⚠️ Не используй must для советов — звучит как приказ!

questions.text: You ___ email the lecturer straight away.
questions.hint: "should" + BASE form. No changes for any subject.

questions.text: You ___ wait until the deadline — start today!

questions.hint: "should" + BASE form only. No -s, no to, no -ing.
"should" = a good idea / recommended, but not a strict rule.

questions.text: "Should" and "must" have the same level of obligation.
questions.hint: "must" is stronger (strict rule); "should" is softer (advice / recommendation).

questions.text: "I ___ you should talk to the lecturer."
questions.hint: "I think you should..." = a common and polite advice phrase.

questions.text: You really ___ (not/leave) your essay to the last minute.
"Should I go in person or email?" — "___, an email is fine."
questions.hint: Short answer to "Should I go in person?": No, you shouldn't (go in person).

questions.text: Students ___ arrive on time — it is expected behaviour.
questions.hint: "Expected behaviour" (not a strict punishable rule) → use "should".

questions.text: "You should to study" is correct grammar.
questions.hint: Never use "to" after modal verbs: "You should study" ✓.

questions.text: She ___ sleep more — she looks exhausted.
questions.hint: "should" + BASE form. No changes for any subject, including she/he/it.

questions.text: Maybe you ___ (not / stress) — two weeks is enough time.

questions.hint: Question: Should + subject + BASE form. No "do" needed.
